html:
The forced merging of the Soviet Union's peasant farms into large collective farms, carried out under Joseph Stalin from about 1928 to the late 1930s.

After the revolution most land was farmed by small peasant households, who sold grain to the state when the price suited them. Stalin wanted cheap grain to feed the cities. Collective farms, the kolkhozes, would make peasants deliver it on the state's terms.

From 1929 the campaign was pushed through by force. Better off peasants, branded kulaks, were shot, sent to labour camps or deported to remote regions, a campaign called dekulakisation. Many peasants slaughtered their animals rather than hand them over.

The state kept seizing grain even as harvests fell. The result was famine in 1932 and 1933, in Ukraine (the Holodomor), in Kazakhstan (the Kazakh famine) and in the Volga and North Caucasus. Millions died. By the end of the 1930s nearly all farming was collective, and Soviet farming stayed weak for the rest of the Union's life.
sum: The forced merging of the Soviet Union's peasant farms into large collective farms, carried out under Joseph Stalin from about 1928 to the late 1930s.
